newsitem.title: USA: Georgia loses 5,600 jobs in September.
newsitem.headline: Georgia loses 5,600 jobs in September.

text.p: Georgia lost 5,600 jobs in September, putting its employment total at 3.55 million, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said Monday.
The September decrease followed the loss of 37,000 jobs in August due to the closing of the Summer Olympics.

"Almost all of the job loss was among temporary workers in restaurants and bars," Poythress said. "Some of these businesses have closed their doors now that the Olympic Games are over, while others are cutting back as they adjust to the post-Olympic environment."
Poythress predicted the state's economy would remain strong, although job growth has begun to slow, especially among temporary workers.

"Permanent job losses, however, are not expected to be widespread in any industries. But some companies seem to be taking stock of the eocnomic environment before embarking on any new projects," Poythress said.
In the past year, Georgia has added 99,900 jobs for a growth rate of 2.9 percent.

Among major urban areas, Athens lost 1,300 jobs in September and Atlanta lost 6,200. Albany gained 100 jobs, August added 1,900, Culumbus added 700, Macon added 1,100 jobs and Savannah added 1,400 jobs in September.
